lede.headline: America votes tomorrow, and the Gulf is watching
lede.summary: Washington has reportedly told Gulf states to prepare for renewed strikes on Iran after the election. Meanwhile, talks in Doha are trying to reopen Hormuz first.
lede.oneBreath: The real question this week is whether the Doha talks deliver before Washington turns back to Iran.

stories.headline: Iran offers to reopen Hormuz in 48 hours, on its terms
stories.brief: Iran and Qatari mediators propose that the US lift sanctions and meet other demands on day one, and Iran reopens the strait on day two. Washington hasn't accepted, and Trump says he is in no hurry.
stories.say: It's faster than anything Tehran has offered, but it's still a list of demands.

more.background: The US and Israel struck Iran on 28 February. A June truce brokered by Pakistan and Qatar collapsed in July, and sanctions returned. Iran also wants a smaller US military presence and its frozen funds released.
more.askThem: Do you think Washington would trade sanctions relief for shipping before the election is even counted?
more.watch: Any US reply through the mediators this week, and whether talk of post-election strikes fades or grows.

stories.headline: US midterms tomorrow: House leans Democratic, Senate too close to call
stories.brief: Forecasts give Democrats about an 80% chance of the House. In the Senate, Republicans hold 53 seats and Democrats need a net gain of four.
stories.say: The House looks settled. Watch the Senate, where half a dozen races are within the margin of error.

more.background: Midterms usually go against the president's party, and polls show voters want a check on Trump. Close Senate races include North Carolina, Maine, Alaska, Ohio, Texas, Iowa and Kansas.
more.askThem: If Democrats take the House, do you expect them to govern or mostly investigate?
more.watch: East Coast polls close in the early hours of Wednesday, Dubai time. The Senate may take days.

stories.headline: Israel's election ends in deadlock
stories.brief: Netanyahu's bloc has 53 seats and Eisenkot's 48, with 61 needed. Likud claims the vote was stolen, while police say there is no evidence and officials say the results stand.
stories.say: Neither side can reach 61 without breaking a promise, so another election is a real possibility.

more.background: Arab-led parties won 19 seats, but Eisenkot has ruled out governing with them. Results must be certified by 4 November, after which President Herzog chooses who tries first to form a government.
more.askThem: Do you think Eisenkot would ever govern with Arab parties' support, even from outside the coalition?
more.watch: Certification by Wednesday, then Herzog's consultations and who is tasked first.

stories.headline: $6.3 billion stolen from Binance
stories.brief: It is the largest crypto theft on record, most of it taken in about twenty minutes. Blockchain analysts link it to North Korea, though the FBI hasn't said so publicly.
stories.say: This was a state operation against the world's biggest exchange.

more.background: TRM Labs and Chainalysis name TraderTraitor, the North Korean group the FBI blamed for last year's $1.5 billion Bybit theft. Binance has frozen about $3 billion and says it will cover all losses.
more.askThem: Does this change how you think about keeping money on exchanges?
more.watch: A formal FBI attribution, and how much of the frozen $3 billion is recovered.

stories.headline: Stocks slip for a third week; oil eases to about $110
stories.brief: Weak tech results have revived doubts about AI spending, and the Fed may raise rates in December. This week brings Apple, AMD and the US jobs report on Friday.
stories.say: The market wants returns on AI now, not promises.

more.background: Brent hit $117 last week. Goldman estimates about $27 of the price is a war-risk premium. The Fed held rates at 3.75–4.00%, with two officials voting for a hike.
more.askThem: Do you think this is a pause in the AI trade or the start of a proper reset?
more.watch: The October jobs report on Friday 6 November, and oil's reaction to any Hormuz news.
